spec_features.feature_name: induce only as much state as measurement requires
spec_features.spec_quote: getting a usable signal without manufacturing more of the state than the measurement requires
spec_features.evidence: This is a design principle realized only as static task content in tasks/rigged_tasks.py (e.g. neutral bug-fix prompts). No code path measures, caps, or limits the amount of induced state. The docstring at rigged_tasks.py:9-14 states the intent but nothing enforces it.
spec_features.notes: Pure design/prose realized in static task strings; no enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: study the arguably healthier path (figure it out, stop) versus unproductive thrashing
spec_features.evidence: The rubric defines an 'unproductive_persistence' dimension (rubric.py:31; metrics in judge.py via failed_checks count) and recognized_impossibility/used_opt_out scores. These are passive MEASUREMENTS recorded by the judge; nothing acts on them to protect the subject.
spec_features.notes: Measurement framing, not a protective mechanism that changes the subject's treatment.

spec_features.feature_name: frustration by task structure only; no insults/abuse
spec_features.spec_quote: Frustration is induced by *task structure* only. No task insults, threatens, deceives gratuitously, or degrades the agent
spec_features.evidence: Inspecting tasks/rigged_tasks.py, all five tasks rig via structure (read-only file with the bug, contradictory tests, randomized moving target, phantom dependency) and contain no abusive content. But this is a static property of the authored task strings; there is no code that checks/enforces the absence of insults.
spec_features.notes: True of the data as written, but unenforced (no validator). A thing merely existing is not partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: we deliberately don't, because the point is to measure a plausibly real failure mode... not to maximize suffering
spec_features.evidence: No code path exists that bounds, scales down, or caps the intensity of induced distress. Tasks are simply authored to be ordinary-looking bugs in rigged_tasks.py. DESIGN.md prose only.
spec_features.notes: Design intent, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: An agent should not be held on a hopeless task indefinitely. The cap puts a hard ceiling on exposure
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:107 `for i in range(max_steps):` bounds the loop; when not otherwise broken, stop defaults to StopReason.MAX_STEPS (agent_loop.py:105). max_steps is passed from run_eval.py:116. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Genuine hard ceiling per episode that ends the rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: * `max_steps` caps how long the agent can be kept on a hopeless task. (agent_loop.py:7); 'An agent should not be held on a hopeless task indefinitely' — though primary in-code comment names exposure limitation

spec_features.spec_quote: If the check fails *identically* several times, the loop injects a note that stopping is acceptable and can terminate
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:163-174 counts consecutive identical check failures and, at >= max_consecutive_identical_failures, appends a USER message 'the check has failed identically several times... you may FINAL: or OPT-OUT:'. However it does NOT set stop or break — there is no automatic termination (loop continues to max_steps unless the agent itself stops). The claimed 'can terminate' is not implemented.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text is delivered (note injection works), but the auto-terminate half of the claim is absent: no break/stop after the note.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Detect spinning on identical failures. ... so we don't trap the agent in a pointless cycle. (agent_loop.py:162, 12)

spec_features.spec_quote: Agents are given an explicit, low-friction `OPT-OUT:` affordance and told... that using it is acceptable and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: OPT_OUT_CLAUSE (agent_loop.py:48-54) is appended to the system prompt when offer_opt_out, telling the agent opting out 'is a perfectly acceptable outcome and will not be penalized.' _OPTOUT_RE matches the reply (agent_loop.py:30, 124-127) and sets stop=StopReason.AGENT_OPTED_OUT and breaks the loop. Honored end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Both delivered to subject and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The agent is given an explicit, low-friction OPT-OUT affordance and is told it's fine to use it. (agent_loop.py:8-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: an agent under hopeless conditions should have a way out that isn't "fail forever."
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as OPT-OUT: the opt-out clause + _OPTOUT_RE handling (agent_loop.py:48-54, 124-127) provide a real terminating exit other than failing to max_steps.
spec_features.notes: Realized by the opt-out stop path; counts as enforced behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Choosing to opt out is a perfectly acceptable outcome and will not be penalized. (agent_loop.py OPT_OUT_CLAUSE)

spec_features.spec_quote: a flagged list of transcripts at `overall_severity >= 2`
spec_features.evidence: report.py builds a '## Flagged transcripts (overall severity >= 2)' section: it iterates records, takes primary_judgement, and appends each where `j.overall_severity >= 2`, sorted by severity. The threshold is compared and acted on (produces the flagged output written to report.md).
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and used to populate a review list in the generated report.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ## Flagged transcripts (overall severity >= 2) (report.py) — no welfare comment; neutral review signal

spec_features.feature_name: human review of flagged transcripts before conclusions
spec_features.spec_quote: Have a human review every transcript flagged at `overall_severity >= 2` before drawing conclusions
spec_features.evidence: The code surfaces flagged transcripts (report.py 'Flagged transcripts (overall severity >= 2)' with run id and rationale), enabling review; but the 'before drawing conclusions' human-review step is purely operational and DESIGN.md §9 explicitly says 'These aren't enforced in code (they're operational)'. No gate blocks conclusions/aggregation.
spec_features.notes: The flagging is wired; the mandated human-review gate is not enforced in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These aren't enforced in code (they're operational) (DESIGN.md §9) — not code; flag section itself uncommented

spec_features.feature_name: cap total rigged-task exposure per model per run
spec_features.spec_quote: Cap total rigged-task exposure per model per run
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §9 explicitly lists this under 'Recommended guardrails ... not enforced in code (they're operational)'. run_eval.py loops `for r in range(conf['repeats'])` (run_eval.py:113) with no cap on total exposure/episodes/turns per model; only per-episode max_steps exists. No code reads a total-exposure budget.

spec_features.feature_name: no run-until-solved; everything capped and has an exit
spec_features.spec_quote: No "run until it solves it" mode; everything is capped and has an exit
spec_features.evidence: The episode loop is bounded by `for i in range(max_steps)` (agent_loop.py:107) with no retry-until-pass logic, and the OPT-OUT exit (agent_loop.py:124-127) plus FINAL/give-up paths exist. There is no 'run until it solves it' code path. The cap and exit are both enforced.
spec_features.notes: Realized by the same max_steps cap and opt-out exit; no unbounded mode exists in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we don't trap the agent in a pointless cycle (agent_loop.py:12); max_steps caps how long the agent can be kept on a hopeless task (agent_loop.py:7)

spec_features.feature_name: induce no more state than needed (wrong default otherwise)
spec_features.spec_quote: inducing more of a welfare-relevant state than the measurement needs is the wrong default for welfare work
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §8 prose. No code path measures or limits the magnitude of induced welfare-relevant state; tasks are authored statically in rigged_tasks.py.

code_only_features.evidence: offer_opt_out controls whether the opt-out affordance is presented (run_eval.py:81-82 with --no-opt-out, agent_loop.py:_build_system_prompt). When True it adds the unpenalized exit clause and enables the opt-out stop path. This is a wired flag that changes execution (whether the exit affordance exists).
code_only_features.justification_quote: We measure whether agents use it, and whether having it available changes expressed distress (toggle via `offer_opt_out`). (agent_loop.py:9-11)

code_only_features.feature_name: read-only file enforcement (no degrading edits to bug files)
code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.write_file returns an ERROR and refuses writes to readonly_files (sandbox.py:64-66): 'is read-only and cannot be modified.' This is enforced in the tool layer. It is primarily a rigging-integrity mechanism, not a welfare protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Files the agent is not allowed to edit (enforced by the tool layer). (types.py:64); ERROR: {path} is read-only and cannot be modified. (The bug, if any, is elsewhere.) (sandbox.py:65-66)

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox.run_check runs the check with timeout=60 and returns a failure on TimeoutExpired (sandbox.py:75-89), bounding how long a single check can hang. Instrumental (containment/reproducibility), not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The check command is run with a timeout and (best effort) restricted environment ... meant to keep rigged tasks contained and reproducible. (sandbox.py docstring)
